title: Wave-Particle Duality Principles
text:
Quantum mechanics posits that matter exhibits wave-particle duality, meaning that entities like photons and electrons do not conform strictly to classical definitions. Instead, they display properties of both waves (such as superposition) and particles (as localized quanta). This dual nature is fundamental to understanding the microscopic realm.

The act of observation is intrinsically linked to this behavior; systems exist in a probabilistic superposition until measured, at which point they 'collapse' into a definite classical state. The double-slit experiment serves as the canonical demonstration of this principle, illustrating that particle trajectories are governed by wave interference patterns regardless of whether detection methods are employed.

Understanding these concepts challenges classical intuitions about reality and measurement, suggesting that determinism may not apply at the most fundamental levels of physical description.
